style: mid-90s east coast hardcore rap, 92 BPM, female MC lead: low husky alto, Queens accent, tough and amused, clipped staccato rapped delivery that bites the last word of every bar, spoken cadence, no melody, swaggering like she's running the class; small crew of male voices barking back each number from the back of the room; hard compressed drum break, cracking dry snare pushed loud, gritty 12-bit sampler grit, short minor-key horn stab hit on every new rule, deep round sub bass, dusty vinyl hiss, sparse and menacing
exclude: singing, melodic hook, auto-tune, trap hi-hats, 808 rolls, pop chorus, choir, male lead vocal, reverb wash, EDM
lyrics:
[Intro: female MC, low and amused, drums drop in]
Uh. Uh-huh.
Money printer manual. Page one. Take notes.

[Verse: rapped, staccato, horn stab on each number, male crew shouts the number back]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[horn stab, crew shouts the number]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[horn stab, crew shouts the number]
Number six: no credit? Nah, they live on the slate,
and you're paying it back in the price on your plate.

[horn stab, crew shouts the number]
Number seven: keep the family out the business,
Treasury and the bank in one bed, God as my witness.

[horn stab, crew shouts the number]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: beat cuts to bass only, she speaks it, dry]
And the fix, from the future? Easy.
No hand on the printer.

[End: snare hit, silence]
